p1-v1.alt: A rocket lifts off on a big flame above clouds of smoke, under a dark blue sky.

textos.texto: In 1972, Pioneer 10 lifted off: the first mission to the outer planets. It was designed to last only 21 months.

p1-v2.alt: The Pioneer 10 probe, with its big white antenna, moves between asteroids of all sizes.

textos.texto: No one knew if a spacecraft could cross the asteroid belt. Pioneer 10 was the first to try.
Deep breath… here I go!

p1-v3.alt: Pioneer 10 flies past Jupiter, a huge planet with colored bands and the Great Red Spot.

textos.texto: In December 1973, it flew about 130,000 km from Jupiter and sent photos of details like the Great Red Spot.
Look at that! No one had been this close.

p1-v4.alt: Lilac-colored Pioneer 11 leaves Earth with a trail behind it; Pioneer 10 waits in the distance.

textos.texto: In 1973, when Pioneer 10 had already crossed the asteroid belt, its twin lifted off: Pioneer 11.
You opened the way! I'll go even farther: to Saturn.
Safe travels, sister!

p2-v1.alt: Pioneer 11 flies close to Saturn and its rings.

textos.texto: In 1979, Pioneer 11 took the first close-up photos of Saturn. It passed about 21,000 km from the planet.
The rings are even prettier up close!

p2-v2.alt: A rectangular golden plaque with engraved drawings: two people, the outline of the probe, a star map and the Sun with its planets.

textos.texto: Each probe carried a metal plaque with a message for whoever finds it: who sent it and where it came from.

p2-v3.alt: Pioneer 10 crosses the line of Neptune's orbit, the blue planet, leaving the other planets' orbits behind.

textos.texto: In 1983, Pioneer 10 crossed the orbit of Neptune, which was then the farthest planet. It was the first human-made object to go that far.
Neptune

p2-v4.alt: The Voyager 1 probe speeds past Pioneer 10.

textos.texto: For many years, Pioneer 10 was the most distant human-made object. In 1998, the faster Voyager 1 overtook it.
Go ahead, Voyager! We showed it could be done.
Thanks for leading the way, Pioneer!

p3-v1.alt: A tiny, distant Pioneer 10 sends radio waves that fade before reaching Earth.

textos.texto: Pioneer 11 sent its last signal in 1995. Pioneer 10 sent its own on January 23, 2003, from more than 12 billion kilometers away: it took over 11 hours to arrive!

p3-v2.alt: A tired-looking Pioneer 10 next to an energy gauge whose needle points to red.

textos.texto: Their power source grew weaker until it could no longer run the transmitter. The probes fell silent.
I can't talk anymore… but I'm still on my way.

p3-v3.alt: Two dotted lines leave the Sun: one takes Pioneer 10 toward a reddish star and the other takes Pioneer 11 toward a group of stars.

textos.texto: Pioneer 10 is traveling toward the star Aldebaran: it will take more than 2 million years to get there. Pioneer 11 is heading toward the constellation Aquila and will pass near one of its stars in about 4 million years.
Aldebaran
Aquila

p3-v4.alt: Pioneer 10 travels in front of the Milky Way; the golden plaque with the message shines beside it.

textos.texto: They no longer send signals, but they keep traveling with a message from Earth.
Silence is not the end: it is the journey.

cierre.datoReal: Pioneer 10's last signal took more than 11 hours to reach Earth, even though it traveled at the speed of light!
cierre.preguntaAula: If you had to draw a message for someone on another planet, what would you put on it?
